description: baseline torch.geqrf implementation for linalg/qr_v2

Replace torch.geqrf with a CUDA C++ batched Householder QR path specialized for the dominant n=512 batch=640 cases, one block group per matrix panel with FP32 compact H/tau output and robust fallback only where required.
CUDA extension rank-trim attempt failed at import because torch load_inline requires ninja in the build environment.
ctypes CUDA tail detector built, but validation guard rejected explicit CUDA stream references.
CUDA C++ detector trims n=512 rank-deficient/clustered inputs to shorter torch.geqrf panels and reassembles compact H/tau; preserves fallback for dense and larger shapes.
Native CUDA assembly plus rank-256 clustered trim validated but regressed clustered benchmark because sqrt-eps transition columns prevented the fast path.
Native CUDA assembly with rank-258 clustered trim validates but is marginally slower than PyTorch slice assignment because zero allocation dominates.

Best result 109339.817 us at commit 0af592d7 (about 1.074x faster than 117450.379 us baseline). Working path is a CUDA C++ ctypes tail detector for n=512 that trims rankdef to 384 columns and clustered to 258 columns before torch.geqrf, then returns full compact H/tau; dense/mixed/general cases fall back. Tried native CUDA assembly and rank-256 clustered trimming, but they regressed; next brief could target true full Householder panel kernels or extend reduced-rank detection to n=1024 nearrank.

Combine worker 1's small-n CUDA C++ QR fast paths for n=32/176 with worker 0's n=512 reduced-rank/clustered-column detector, preserving disjoint shape dispatch so small dense cases use custom kernels, detected n=512 cases trim/reassemble around torch.geqrf, and all other dense/large cases fall back unchanged.
Combined worker1 n=32/176 CUDA QR kernels with worker0 n=512 CUDA C++ tail detector and reduced-rank geqrf reassembly; disjoint dispatch validates and improves geomean.
Attempted to fold the n=512 tail detector into worker1 load_inline extension, but CUDA compile failed because C10_CUDA_KERNEL_LAUNCH_CHECK was unavailable in that source.
Unified load_inline extension for small QR and n=512 tail detector validates, but benchmark is slightly slower than the separate ctypes detector combine.

Best combine result 99225.955 us at commit 6441e94e, stacking worker1 n=32/176 CUDA QR kernels with worker0 n=512 rankdef/clustered CUDA tail detector and reduced-rank geqrf reassembly. This beats worker1 alone (106444.537 us) and worker0 alone (109339.817 us). Unified load_inline tail detector validated but was slightly slower at 99295.358 us; keep the separate ctypes detector unless simplifying packaging is more important. Next brief could target n=352 custom QR or n=1024 nearrank/rank trim, since the current combine leaves those fallback paths unchanged.

Tune the existing n=32 and n=176 CUDA C++ QR kernels from 6441e94e by profiling register pressure, occupancy, and barrier stalls, then sweep only block shape, unroll depth, and necessary __syncthreads placement; keep dispatch and n=512 reduced-rank detector behavior unchanged.
Swept n=32 to 32 threads and n=176 to 128 threads; n=32 improved but n=176 slowed enough to regress geomean.
Changed only the n=32 small QR kernel from 64 to 32 threads while keeping n=176 and n=512 behavior unchanged; improves geomean and n=32 latency.
Removed tau-zero conditionals in the n=32/176 QR update path after retaining n=32 one-warp launch; validation passes and geomean improves slightly.
Swept n=176 from 256 to 512 threads with n=32 one-warp/no-branch changes; validation passed but n=176 latency regressed heavily.

Best micro result 98668.785 us at commit f29d05a4, tuning only the existing small CUDA QR kernels: n=32 launch changed from 64 to 32 threads and tau-zero branches removed from the update path while n=176 dispatch remains 256 threads and n=512 behavior unchanged. Sweeps showed n=176 at 128 threads regressed to 99319.176 us and n=176 at 512 threads regressed to 101408.268 us. Final profile captured for f29d05a4; further work should likely target deeper n=176 algorithmic/barrier changes rather than block count.

Profile torch.geqrf for the batch=8 n=2048 benchmark, then implement an n=2048-only CUDA C++ library-backed geqrf wrapper or blocked compact-Householder path behind dispatch to reduce overhead, keeping this baseline-diverse branch independent from existing n=32/176, n=512, and n=1024 fast paths.
n=2048 cuSOLVER geqrf wrapper built but failed validation with NaNs in materialized Q, likely from row-major/column-major layout mismatch.
Added n=2048-only cuSOLVER geqrf wrapper with CUDA transpose pack/unpack to correct row-major layout; validation passes and geomean is a tiny improvement over baseline.
Cached cuSOLVER handle and geqrf buffer size for the n=2048 packed wrapper; validation passes and n=2048 timing improves slightly versus the first valid wrapper.

Best n=2048 baseline-diverse result 117364.114 us at commit b6f8ca97. Implemented a CUDA C++/cuSOLVER n=2048-only dispatch with CUDA transpose pack/unpack to satisfy row-major compact-H semantics and cached the cuSOLVER handle/buffer size. The first direct cuSOLVER attempt failed validation due layout mismatch; the packed wrapper validated and gave only a small gain because transpose overhead mostly cancels cuSOLVER savings. Next work should likely combine this only if independent gains matter, or pursue a true row-major blocked Householder kernel to avoid pack/unpack.

Combine the current global-best CUDA dispatch with the isolated n=2048 cuSOLVER-backed QR wrapper; add it only behind an exact n=2048 shape gate, preserve all existing n=32/176, n=512, n=1024, n=4096 if present, and mixed-batch fast paths, and remove or bypass it if dispatch overhead or library setup regresses other shapes.
Added isolated n=2048 cuSOLVER pack/unpack dispatch to current global-best, preserving existing gates; validation passes but benchmark regresses versus parent, so it should be bypassed.
Bypassed the n=2048 cuSOLVER wrapper after measured regression; keeps current global-best dispatch unchanged as best state for this combine brief.
Measured the bypassed/global-best state after removing the n=2048 wrapper; score is within noise of parent and remains better than the combined wrapper attempt.

Combine brief exhausted. Adding the isolated n=2048 cuSOLVER pack/unpack wrapper to global-best validated but regressed to 97050.025 us, so it was bypassed. Best final state keeps global-best dispatch unchanged and measured 96960.097 us at commit 1b6f5bc3 (empty marker atop parent 20acd6f); this is within noise of parent 96942.416 and better than the n=2048 wrapper combine. Recommendation: do not merge the n=2048 cuSOLVER path into global-best unless a later row-major/no-pack implementation removes the transpose overhead.

Specialize the n=32 QR path with a warp-resident unrolled CUDA C++ Householder panel kernel that preserves geqrf A/tau semantics while reducing launch, global-memory, and index overhead; compare against the current n=32 kernel and keep only if validation and benchmark improve.
Warp-shuffle n=32 QR rewrite built but failed n=32 factor residual validation, likely missing memory ordering between per-column warp updates.
Synchronized warp-shuffle n=32 QR rewrite still failed n=32 factor residual validation; preserving geqrf semantics needs more than this direct warp rewrite.
Replaced n=32 small QR dispatch with a warp-resident CUDA C++ Householder kernel using shuffle reductions with lane-0 broadcast; validation passes and n=32 latency drops substantially.
Removed per-column warp syncs from the validated warp-resident n=32 QR kernel; validation still passes and n=32/geomean improve slightly.

Tried unrolling the warp-resident n=32 QR panel loops and removed the redundant matrix guard; validation passes but benchmark regresses versus the no-inner-sync best, so this variant should not be kept.

Brief exhausted. Best n=32 warp-resident CUDA C++ Householder kernel result is 94566.569 us at commit 472716bb731da62eae5b64a3ce40093ffb5d3aa4. Valid fix required broadcasting warp reduction results from lane 0; removing inner per-column syncs then improved slightly. Final unroll/guard-removal variant validated but regressed to 94804.467 us, so the branch was restored to the no-inner-sync best. Final nsys profile captured for the best commit; further gains likely require work outside this n=32 brief.

Explore isolated n=352 batch=40 cuSOLVER geqrf substitution from baseline, including row/column-major pack/unpack and workspace reuse; profile whether library QR beats torch.geqrf for this shape, abandon if transpose/setup overhead dominates, and do not touch global-best dispatch unless full active validation/benchmark improves.
Added isolated n=352 cuSOLVER geqrf path with CUDA row/column pack and unpack plus cached handle/lwork; full validation passes and benchmark is a small improvement over baseline.
Cached fixed-size cuSOLVER workspace and info tensors for the isolated n=352 path; validation passes and geomean improves slightly versus the first wrapper.
Tried replacing the linear n=352 pack/unpack transpose with a tiled shared-memory transpose, but validation failed on the n=352 test with NaNs in H.
Corrected the tiled n=352 transpose to cover all tile rows; validation passes but benchmark regresses versus the cached linear transpose, so it should not be kept.

Brief exhausted. Best isolated n=352 cuSOLVER substitution is commit 29d773a670c3a666bf93bb39a05569aec9866c52 with linalg/qr_v2=116861.309 us, improving baseline 117450.379 us slightly. The path uses CUDA row/column pack and unpack plus cached cuSOLVER handle, lwork, work tensor, and info tensor. A corrected tiled transpose validated but regressed to 117133.070 us, and an initial tiled attempt failed validation with NaNs, so the best state restores the cached linear transpose. Final nsys profile captured for the best commit; library QR only marginally beats torch.geqrf for n=352 because transpose/setup and per-matrix calls dominate.

Selectively combine d57 global-best QR paths with the isolated n=352 batch=40 cuSOLVER geqrf pack/unpack implementation behind an exact shape gate, preserving existing n=32, n=176, n=512, n=1024, and fallback dispatch behavior while evaluating whether the library path improves that active shape without disturbing other paths.
Combined d57 global-best QR dispatch with the isolated cached n=352 cuSOLVER pack/unpack path behind an exact (352,352) gate; validation passes and benchmark improves to 90534.560 us.

Combine brief exhausted. Best and final state is commit 41cb548c7a8f0a751f15bfcea613d7e228888c7f with linalg/qr_v2=90534.560 us, improving parent d57ae92's 90576.984 us slightly. The change selectively adds the cached n=352 cuSOLVER geqrf pack/unpack path behind an exact (352,352) gate while preserving d57 n=32, n=176, n=512, n=1024, and fallback dispatch behavior. Full validation passed; final nsys profile captured. The n=352 shape was slightly slower than the isolated parent run but the full geomean still improved within noise, so this combine is worth keeping unless manager wants a repeat measurement.

Starting from d018 global best, integrate only 41cb's exact-gated n=352 cached cuSOLVER pack/unpack dispatch path, preserving d018's n=176 four-warp kernel, sync-free n=32 path, n=512/n=1024 paths, homogeneous fast paths, and fallbacks; isolate behavioral changes to n=352.

Integrated 41cb's exact-gated cached n=352 cuSOLVER pack/unpack dispatch into d018 global-best while preserving d018 n=32, n=176, n=512, n=1024, homogeneous fast paths, and fallbacks; full validation passes and benchmark improves to 89945.706 us.

Combine brief exhausted. Best and final state is commit 03ce8a57a973be0296643110090dd3f07206c1f1 with linalg/qr_v2=89945.706 us, improving d01879 parent 90097.449 us while isolating behavior changes to n=352. The change adds only 41cb's exact-gated cached n=352 cuSOLVER geqrf pack/unpack dispatch and preserves d018's n=32 sync-free kernel, n=176 four-warp kernel, n=512/n=1024 paths, homogeneous fast paths, and fallbacks. Full validation passed and final nsys profile was captured.

Explore an n=512 rank-def/clustered custom CUDA C++ prefix QR path replacing torch.geqrf only for exact detected reduced-rank cases, starting with rank-384 prefixes via blocked Householder panel/update kernels; preserve 03ce dispatch for n=32/n=176/n=352/n=1024 and dense fallback, generalizing to rank-258 only if the same path is clean.

Added a custom one-block CUDA C++ Householder QR for exact detected n=512 rank-384 prefixes, replacing torch.geqrf in homogeneous and mixed rank-384 reduced paths; validation passes and benchmark improves to 89165.428 us.
Generalized the custom n=512 one-block CUDA prefix QR to rank-258 detected clustered/tiny cases as well as rank-384; validation passes and benchmark improves to 85936.096 us.
Removed the per-column synchronization inside the validated n=512 rank-384/rank-258 CUDA prefix QR update loop; validation still passes and benchmark improves slightly to 85914.620 us.

Restricted the custom n=512 rank-384/rank-258 CUDA prefix QR to homogeneous detected batches while leaving mixed subsets on the existing torch.geqrf gather/scatter path; validation passes and benchmark improves to 85474.782 us.

Brief exhausted. Best result is commit 34723e8d368041c8ebe2d032df0031dab83fe0f4 with linalg/qr_v2=85474.782 us. Added a custom CUDA C++ one-block Householder prefix QR for n=512 rank-384 and rank-258 homogeneous detected batches, removed the inner per-column sync after validation, and kept mixed subsets on the existing torch.geqrf gather/scatter path because custom subset QR slowed mixed n=512. Iterations: rank-384 only 89165.428 us, rank-258 mixed-capable 85936.096 us, no-inner-sync 85914.620 us, homogeneous-only best 85474.782 us. Full validation passed and final nsys profile captured.

Profile the homogeneous n=512 rank-384/rank-258 CUDA prefix-QR path in 34723e, identify the single hottest stall or memory bottleneck, and tune exactly one kernel-local choice such as panel tile, unroll depth, warp ownership, or tau/shared layout; preserve homogeneous-only dispatch, keep mixed n=512 on torch.geqrf, and leave all other n fallbacks unchanged.

Tuned the homogeneous n=512 rank-384/rank-258 CUDA prefix QR kernel-local block width from 256 to 128 threads while preserving homogeneous-only dispatch and all fallbacks; validation passes and benchmark improves to 85015.013 us.

Continued the same kernel-local block-width sweep for the homogeneous n=512 prefix QR, reducing the block from 128 to 64 threads while keeping dispatch unchanged; validation passes and benchmark improves to 84835.997 us.

Micro brief exhausted. Tuned exactly one kernel-local bottleneck in the homogeneous n=512 rank-384/rank-258 CUDA prefix QR path: block width / reduction ownership. Preserved homogeneous-only dispatch, kept mixed n=512 on torch.geqrf, and left all other n fallbacks unchanged. Parent 34723e measured 85474.782 us; 128-thread block validated and improved to 85015.013 us; 64-thread block validated and improved further to 84835.997 us at commit c3b4be68c612fef883ddcdeca6d05073cd65be0e. Final nsys profile captured.

Combine c3b4 + 3b597: starting from c3b4, port only 3b597's n=1024 rank-768 zero-tail CUDA C++ reassembly after torch.geqrf prefix, including contiguous prefix-factor handling. Preserve c3b4's n512 64-thread homogeneous prefix QR/mixed torch.geqrf dispatch, n352 cuSOLVER, n176/n32 kernels, n1024 dense/mixed fallbacks, and all non-n1024 behavior unchanged; reject any broader classifier or dispatch rewrite.

Ported only 3b597's n=1024 rank-768 zero-tail CUDA C++ reassembly after torch.geqrf prefix into the c3b4 branch, with contiguous h/tau prefix-factor handling and unchanged c3b4 dispatch outside the homogeneous zero-tail gate; validation passes but benchmark regresses to 85847.949 us versus parent 84835.997 us.

Removed only the explicit torch.cuda.synchronize calls around the ported n=1024 rank-768 reassembly helper while preserving the c3b4 dispatch and reassembly gate; validation passes but benchmark remains regressed at 85573.022 us versus parent 84835.997 us.

Combine brief exhausted. Starting from c3b4, I surgically ported only 3b597's n=1024 rank-768 zero-tail CUDA C++ reassembly after the torch.geqrf prefix, including contiguous h/tau prefix-factor handling, while preserving c3b4 dispatch exactly outside that homogeneous zero-tail gate. The exact port validated but regressed to 85847.949 us versus parent 84835.997 us; a narrower no-explicit-synchronize variant also validated but regressed to 85573.022 us. Reset HEAD back to the better c3b4 parent; no final combined improvement retained.

From c3b4, profile homogeneous n512 rank-384 and rank-258 separately; if bottlenecks differ, add one minimal rank-specific CUDA block-width/kernel choice for exactly one rank while leaving the other on the current 64-thread kernel. Preserve homogeneous-only dispatch, mixed n512 torch.geqrf, and all n352/n176/n32/n1024/n4096 paths unchanged; revert if either rank regresses.

Tried exactly one rank-specific n512 CUDA kernel choice: rank-258 uses a 32-thread block while rank-384 remains on the c3b4 64-thread block; homogeneous-only dispatch and all non-rank258 paths unchanged. Full validation passed, but benchmark regressed to 85056.498 us versus parent 84835.997 us.

Tried exactly one rank-specific n512 CUDA kernel choice: rank-384 uses a 32-thread block while rank-258 is restored to the c3b4 64-thread block; homogeneous-only dispatch and all non-rank384 paths unchanged. Full validation passed, but benchmark regressed to 84960.116 us versus parent 84835.997 us.

Tried exactly one rank-specific n512 CUDA kernel choice: rank-258 uses a 128-thread block while rank-384 remains on the c3b4 64-thread block; homogeneous-only dispatch and all non-rank258 paths unchanged. Full validation passed, but benchmark regressed to 85451.633 us versus parent 84835.997 us.

Tried exactly one rank-specific n512 CUDA kernel choice: rank-384 uses a 128-thread block while rank-258 is restored to the c3b4 64-thread block; homogeneous-only dispatch and all non-rank384 paths unchanged. Full validation passed, but benchmark regressed to 85179.624 us versus parent 84835.997 us.

Micro brief exhausted. Profile inspection did not reveal a separable n512 templated-kernel bottleneck in the parent nsys summary, so I exhaustively tested minimal rank-specific block-width choices while preserving homogeneous-only dispatch, mixed n512 torch.geqrf, and every non-target path. Rank-258 at 32 threads validated but regressed to 85056.498 us; rank-384 at 32 threads validated but regressed to 84960.116 us; rank-258 at 128 threads validated but regressed to 85451.633 us; rank-384 at 128 threads validated but regressed to 85179.624 us. Reset HEAD to c3b4 because parent 64/64 remains best at 84835.997 us; no final rank-specific change retained.

From 1567, add an exact-gated dense homogeneous n512 fast path that skips rank detection, masks, gather/scatter, and mixed-batch logic, routing directly to the fastest existing QR backend for contiguous dense n512; preserve rank-384/rank-258 custom QR, mixed n512, n352/n176/n32/n1024/n4096 behavior, and abandon unless dense n512 and geomean improve.

Added an exact all-dense homogeneous n512 gate after the existing n512 CUDA flag pass: if no rank-384/rank-258 flags are present, route directly to torch.geqrf and skip n512 mask/scatter/mixed-batch logic; reduced-rank/mixed/non-n512 behavior remains unchanged. Full validation passed, but benchmark was 85226.607 us and did not improve the geomean.

Added a dedicated exact all-dense n512 CUDA detector that returns a single byte before the existing rank/mask/gather path, routing all-dense n512 directly to torch.geqrf while preserving reduced-rank/mixed/non-n512 behavior. Full validation passed, but dense n512 and geomean did not improve; benchmark regressed to 85420.887 us.

Macro brief exhausted and abandoned per objective. From 1567, I tested two exact-gated dense homogeneous n512 routes to torch.geqrf while preserving rank-384/rank-258 custom QR, mixed n512, and all non-n512 behavior. Iteration 0 reused existing n512 flags then skipped mask/scatter for all-dense batches; validation passed but benchmark regressed to 85226.607 us. Iteration 1 added a dedicated one-byte all-dense CUDA detector before rank/mask/gather logic; validation passed but benchmark regressed further to 85420.887 us. Reset HEAD to parent 1567f1af because neither dense n512 nor geomean improved.

Profile c3b4 n512 homogeneous rank-384/rank-258 64-thread prefix QR store traffic; if stores are material, exact-gate one rank case to skip redundant zero/trailing writes while preserving required H/tau layout, mixed-n512 torch path, n4096 fast path, and all non-n512 dispatch; abandon on any validation failure or geomean regression.

Tried one exact-gated rank case: rank-384 skips redundant full-H zeroing that is immediately overwritten and only zeros trailing H/tau ranges; rank-258 and dispatch remain unchanged. Full validation passed, but benchmark regressed to 85424.725 us.

Tried the same safe redundant-store skip for the exact rank-258 n512 custom QR case while restoring rank-384 behavior; rank-258 skips H/tau zero writes that are immediately overwritten and still zeros required trailing H/tau ranges. Full validation passed, but benchmark regressed to 85294.914 us.

A first build attempt failed due root-owned .torch_ext lock left by sudo/ncu profiling and was logged/cleaned. Tested one exact-gated redundant-write skip for rank-384: validation passed but geomean regressed to 85424.725 us. Tested the analogous exact-gated skip for rank-258: validation passed but geomean regressed to 85294.914 us. Reset HEAD to parent 1567f1af; no store-skip change retained.
